newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK COURT PUTS OFF TRIAL OF GREENPEACE ACTIVISTS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK COURT PUTS OFF TRIAL OF GREENPEACE ACTIVISTS.

text.p: A Greek court postponed on Thursday the trial of 17 Greenpeace activists on charges stemming from their 24-hour blockade of a major oil refinery.
"We were ready to be tried but the trial didn't take place. Greenpeace demands an immediate trial," said Nikos Charalambidis, a defendant and leader of the refinery action.
The court in the southern Greek city of Corinth put off the trial claiming work overload and will set a new date on Friday, Greenpeace said in a statement.
The defendants could face up to five years in jail if convicted on charges of trespass and hindering a public service company, for blocking the Motor Oil refinery near the Corinth canal in November.

The activists took over the refinery's port to protest over a major spill at the docking facilities in August. They were forcibly removed by coast guard commandos, who cut through chains pinning them to mooring buoys and loading cranes.
Political opposition parties had issued strong statements at the time, decrying the military-style operation and questioning the need of sending hooded commandos to deal with peaceful activists.

An estimated 300 tonnes of crude oil was spilled as a tanker owned by Motor Oil was unloading during a thunderstorm in the middle of the night. A lightning bolt struck dead a worker and the ship was detached from its moorings, breaking its loading pipe.
Motor Oil, jointly owned by Saudi Aramco and the Greek Vardinoyannis family, was fined 150 million drachmas ($650,000) by the Merchant Marine Ministry for the accident.
"Greenpeace wants this trial because it is Motor Oil that will be essentially tried," Charalambidis said. "They are guilty of a major oil spill and they have not even been charged yet."
Motor Oil has said its safety measures are beyond those required by Greek law and blamed the oil spill on the sudden storm.

Greenpeace wants a ban on loading at night or in bad weather, stricter laws against oil pollution and more prevention measures. It says oil dispersants used after oil spills in Greece are toxic and should be forbidden.
Only the eight Greek defendants appeared in court. Nine foreigners, who include activists from Britain, Austria and Germany will probably appear at the next scheduled date, Charalambidis said.
